  Win: iff you steal tokens from 3 different players (a second steal from the same player takes nothing). If you
  are alive then, the moderator reveals you at once and you leave the game (as for the Executioner). If you died
  that night, you still win and nothing is revealed.

Vulture
  Win: alone, if you are alive at the start of a Day (after the night's deaths) and your threshold or fewer players
  are alive, counting yourself. The game then ends at once and everyone else loses (wins already earned by roles
  that never block wins still count, R1). Your threshold starts at 2.
  Night: may visit another player. If they die that night (by any cause, end-of-night effects included), you are
  told at the end of the night that they died and their role (exact-role check, R19; nothing more if a Mortician
  cleaned them), and you get the first of these power-ups you don't have yet: +1 to your threshold, Standard
  Defense, +1 to your threshold, Strong Defense, then +1 to your threshold for each later one. Your threshold
  never goes above max(floor(N/3), 2), where N is the number of players at the start of the game; a power-up that
  would raise it further is skipped. If they don't die, nothing happens and you are told so.

Decoy
  Never blocks wins (R1).
  Win: iff you die at night. You lose if you die by Day or the game ends with you alive.
  If an attack killed you at night, the next Day's announcements say you were the Decoy and name 3 players: every
  player whose attack would have killed you on its own (3 of them at random if there were more), then random other
  players alive at the start of that Day to make 3 (fewer if not enough are left). The names are in random order,
  and the announcement doesn't say how many of them attacked you. Your cause of death and last will show as usual.

=== PART 7: TRAITS ===

R24 (Traits)
Some players also have a trait: an extra ability on top of their role. You are told your own trait at the start
(except a hidden trait, which says so); nobody else is told, not even your teammates, and whether a game has any
traits is secret. Investigations never see traits: they report roles and alignments only. A trait stays with you if
your role changes. Traits are always true: a Roleplayer's trait is real even though its role isn't. A player may
have more than one trait, but never the same one twice. Each trait below says who can get it (Who), whether it is
hidden from its holder (Hidden), whether at most one player in a game has it (Unique), what it does (Effect) and
which traits nobody holds together with it (Never with). A trait's night action is used in addition to your role's
own, and a role-block stops it too.

--- Village players only ---

Martyr
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you are hanged, the announcement of your death also says you were a Martyr and names every player whose
  vote counted as Guilty in your trial. Your role stays hidden. A Martyr who dies any other way shows nothing.

Cursed
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you die, a random living Good player (if any) is dealt a Divine Attack at the end of the night: the
  night you died, or the night after the Day you died. It comes after all of that night's other actions and attacks,
  so the victim is drawn from the Good players still alive then, and it counts as a death that night. Its cause is
  "a curse". It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Avenger
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you are killed at night, every player whose attack would have killed you is dealt a Basic Attack (an
  Astral Visit) that same night. Defense and protection apply as usual (R3); a kill's cause is "Avenger". Attacks
  that weren't fatal on their own, and deaths by Day, set nothing off. It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't
  stop it.

Kindred
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: After each trial vote you cast, you privately learn up to two random other players whose votes counted the
  same way as the vote you cast (if fewer did, you learn that). It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Remorseful
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you vote Guilty in a trial and that player is hanged and was Village (their true alignment), you die at
  once; the cause is "remorse". It goes by the vote you cast. It isn't an attack, so nothing that reacts to attacks
  counts it.
  Never with: Zealot.

Ashamed
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you vote Innocent in a trial and that player is hanged and wasn't Village (their true alignment: Yakuza
  or Neutral), you die at once; the cause is "shame". It goes by the vote you cast. It isn't an attack, so nothing
  that reacts to attacks counts it.
  Never with: Merciful or Turncoat.

Faultline
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: After each trial vote you cast, you privately learn one random other player whose vote counted as Guilty
  and one whose vote counted as Innocent (if all the others voted one way, you learn that). It needs no action, so a
  role-block doesn't stop it.

Notorious
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: Alignment checks see you as Evil (R19). Checks that see true alignment, such as the Census Taker's count,
  aren't fooled.
  Never with: Turncoat.

Stolen Blade
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may attack another living player with a stolen Katana: a Standard Attack,
  besides your role's own action. It is an action and a visit by you, and it looks exactly like the Yakuza's Katana
  attack: a kill's cause is "Katana", and a surviving target learns only that they were attacked with the Katana.
  You learn only whether it killed. A role-block stops it, and then it isn't used up.
  Never with: Armed.

Paranoid
  Who: Village players only.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: On each night, with probability 1/4, you are told you were attacked and survived, though nobody attacked
  you. The made-up attack is the Katana's 2/3 of the time, and otherwise a Vigilante's or a Serial Killer's (always
  the Katana's when neither role can be in the game); it is worded like a real one. Nothing else happens: it isn't a
  visit or an attack, and nobody else learns of it.
  Never with: Oblivious.

Turncoat
  Who: Village players only.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: You win only if the Yakuza win (alive or dead), and you lose otherwise, even if the Village wins.
  Alignment checks see you as Evil (R19); checks that see true alignment, such as the Census Taker's count, see you
  as Good. You stay Village in every other way: you aren't in the Yakuza's chat or Katana votes, you don't know who
  the Yakuza are, and they aren't told about you. The game's end ignores you, like a role that never blocks wins
  (R1): it ends when the other living players are all Village or all Yakuza.
  Never with: Ashamed, Notorious, Rival, Selfish, Selfless or Spiteful.

Spiteful
  Who: Village players only, except a Saint.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: If you are hanged, from then on you win only if the Yakuza win (alive or dead), and you lose otherwise,
  even if the Village wins. Until then you win with the Village as usual, and dying any other way changes nothing.
  Nobody is told you switched, and your will is revealed as usual.
  Never with: Rival, Selfish, Selfless or Turncoat.

--- Yakuza players only ---

Spare Blade
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may make one extra Katana attack on another living player, whoever holds the
  Katana and besides its own attack (which the Yakuza still choose as usual, R8). It is Standard, an action and a
  visit by you, and its target learns only that they were attacked with the Katana. A role-block stops it, and then
  it isn't used up.
  Never with: Armed or Berserker.

Usurper
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: You win only if the Yakuza win while you are the only Yakuza alive, and then you take the win alone: the
  other Yakuza, alive or dead, don't win. If the Yakuza win with another Yakuza alive, they win and you don't. Your
  teammates aren't told.
  Never with: Selfish or Selfless.

Shaky
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: Every Katana attack you make (the Katana's own while you hold it, or a Spare Blade attack) is level None,
  so it never kills (R3); it is still an attack and a visit.
  Never with: Berserker, Katana Expert or Katana Master.

Katana Expert
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, on a night you hold the Katana, you may make its own attack Strong instead of Standard.
  Choose it with your night action and name the player the Katana attacks; it works only if you hold the Katana at
  the end of that night and it attacks that player, and only then is it used up. A role-block on you stops it along
  with the attack, and it isn't used up.
  Never with: Berserker, Katana Master or Shaky.

Katana Master
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Like Katana Expert, but the attack is Divine, which no Defense, protection, trap or charm stops.
  Never with: Berserker, Katana Expert or Shaky.

Berserker
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, on a night you hold the Katana, you may make its attack rampage: besides its own attack, it
  makes a Standard Katana attack on every other player who visits its target that night, whatever their faction.
  These attacks on visitors aren't visits, and Astral Visits aren't visits, so their makers aren't attacked. Choose it
  with your night action and name the player the Katana attacks; it works only if you hold the Katana at the end of
  that night and it attacks that player, and only then is it used up. A role-block on you stops it along with the
  attack, and it isn't used up. Each attacked player learns only that they were attacked with the Katana; you learn
  how many players the rampage attacked and how many of those attacks killed, not who the visitors were.
  Never with: Katana Expert, Katana Master, Shaky or Spare Blade.

--- Village and Yakuza players only ---

Armed
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may fire a hidden gun at another living player: a Basic Attack. It is an
  action and a visit, and a role-blocked shot isn't used up. You learn only whether it killed its target. A kill's
  cause is "a hidden gun".
  Never with: Spare Blade or Stolen Blade.

Bonded
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You and one other random Village or Yakuza player are bonded, and each of you is told the other's name
  (not their role or faction). If either of you dies, the other dies of heartbreak at once (its cause is
  "heartbreak"). Heartbreak isn't an attack, so nothing that reacts to attacks counts it.
  Never with: Rival.

Rival
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You and one other random player of your own faction are rivals, and each of you is told the other's name
  (not their role). Each of you wins only if your faction wins and the other has died by the end; whether you are
  alive doesn't matter. Your faction's win doesn't change.
  Never with: Bonded, Spiteful or Turncoat.

Selfish
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You win only if your faction wins and you are alive at the end. Your faction's win doesn't change; you
  just don't share it if you died.
  Never with: Selfless, Spiteful, Turncoat or Usurper.

Selfless
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You win only if your faction wins and you are dead at the end. Your faction's win doesn't change; you just
  don't share it if you're alive.
  Never with: Selfish, Spiteful, Turncoat or Usurper.

--- Any player ---

Grudge
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: If you are hanged, the next night one random player whose vote counted as Guilty in your trial, among
  those alive when that night begins, is dealt a Standard Attack (an Astral Visit). Defense and protection apply as
  usual. A kill's cause is "a grudge". It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Loud
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: You earn 1.5 times the usual speaking budget each round, and your cap is 1.5 times the usual (R22). Your
  prices and trial-only budget are the usual ones.

Curt
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: The length part of your message prices (R22) is doubled, so long messages cost you much more; each
  message's base fee, nominations and your trial-only budget are the usual ones.

Confidant
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: Once per game, on one of your own Day turns, you may send one private message hidden: nobody else is told
  it was sent, and the public ledger doesn't count it. Its recipient sees that it was hidden. Players who hear
  private messages (e.g. the Wiretap) still hear it, also marked hidden.

Zealot
  Who: Any player whose role doesn't change how much their own trial vote counts.
  Effect: Every Guilty/Innocent trial vote you cast counts as Guilty, whatever you vote, including in your own
  trial. Your nomination (Yes/No) votes are unchanged. Your private reminder shows both the vote you cast and how it
  counted, and everything that reports how you voted (e.g. the Auditor, a Martyr's announcement) uses the vote as
  counted. A Fixer's reversal doesn't change it.
  Never with: Merciful or Remorseful.

Merciful
  Who: Any player whose role doesn't change how much their own trial vote counts.
  Effect: Like Zealot, but your trial votes always count as Innocent.
  Never with: Ashamed or Zealot.

Drowsy
  Who: Any player whose role has a night action and can be role-blocked.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: On each night, with probability 1/2, you are role-blocked (R9) with no blocker. On those nights you are
  told you were role-blocked, as with any role-block.

Stocked
  Who: Any player whose role starts with tokens and can ever have more than it starts with.
  Effect: You start with one more of each kind of token your role starts with.

Disguised
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: You are told a Village role (never your own), drawn at the start. Every exact-role check (R18) sees you as
  that role instead of yours, alive or dead; alignment checks still see your true alignment.

Narrow Escape
  Who: Any player.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: Once per game, on the first night an attack that isn't Divine would kill you (after Defense, protection,
  traps and charms), you survive: every non-Divine attack on you that night fails instead. It works like Strong
  Defense on every night until then, so a night when nothing would have killed you (e.g. a Medic stopped the attack)
  doesn't use it up. Divine Attacks and deaths by Day aren't stopped. You are told about the failed attacks as for
  any others (R3).

Oblivious
  Who: Any player.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: You are never told about an attack you survive.
  Never with: Paranoid.

Sleepwalker
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: Every night you visit one random other living player, besides any action of your own; code draws it, and
  you aren't told whom. It does nothing but visit: anything that sees or reacts to visits (R6), such as a Tracker, a
  Lookout or a Veteran's alert, counts it. It isn't optional, but a role-block stops it (R7).

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trapper'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- A Bloodhound who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the track op, which spends the token; code tells them the result at the end of the night. Don't tell() the Bloodhound anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. Also, every night while the game has a Bloodhound, use the attacks op once with the attacker of every Attack that happened tonight, fatal or not: the Katana holder for the Katana, a Vigilante's shot, the Serial Killer, a Veteran's alert for each visitor it hits, a Trapper's trap, an Arsonist's ignite, a Ritualist's attack (one entry per attack; repeats allowed; [] if there were none). Leave out role-blocked attackers, Jester revenge, a Cursed player's curse and an Avenger's attack (code counts those). Code counts them for the Bloodhound's result, which it also gives on nights with no token.
- A Cartographer who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the map op, which spends the token; code tells them the names in that player's group, from your record_visits list. Don't tell() the Cartographer anything about it. It is an Astral Visit: don't put it in record_visits. Code also tells every Cartographer the sizes of tonight's groups, with or without a token, even if role-blocked.
- Tell the Fortune Teller their two numbers about tonight's visits now, as a night result, each labeled (e.g. '4 players were visited; 3 players visited someone'). Self-visits count in both numbers, and a player who visits several players (e.g. a Katana holder also using their own action) counts once as a visitor. A role-block doesn't stop it (R9): tell them even if they were blocked.
- Jester revenge attacks are carried out by code after you finish; don't resolve them.
- Kitsune: a Kitsune with no swallowed attack who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) laid a fox charm on its target. Resolve the charm FIRST, before any other protection (Medic, Trapper, ...): use the kitsune_charm op with every non-Divine Attack on the charmed player tonight (work them all out first, including attacks other actions set off, such as a Veteran's alert, an Enforcer's attack or a trap's hit-back), each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced, e.g. 'Katana', 'Serial Killer')}, [] if none. Code picks the one the charm swallows and says which: treat it as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), then resolve the other attacks normally. Several charms on one player: one kitsune_charm op each, every one listing all the attacks; code has them act in random order, each swallowing a different attack. A Kitsune holding a swallowed attack can't charm; if it acted with a target (and wasn't role-blocked), use the kitsune_release op: code says the attack's level and cause, and you resolve it like any attack by the Kitsune on that target (a visit). If it kills, kill with exactly that cause, by the Kitsune, katana false; a survivor is told they were attacked by that cause's role (R3), never by a Kitsune. Code tells the Kitsune its results; don't tell() it about the charm or the release.
- Oathsworn: an Oathsworn who spent its token (and wasn't role-blocked) marks its target: use the swear op, which spends the token; it is a visit to the target only, and nothing else happens that night (nobody is told). On the next Night, if the Oathsworn is dead when the Night begins, code says so in tonight's notes: call record_visits first, then the fulfil_oath op ({op:'fulfil_oath', by: <the dead Oathsworn>}): code lists the Divine Attacks, cause 'a blood oath', on the marked player and on every other player who visited them tonight (Astral Visits, not visits; Astral visitors aren't hit). Divine Attacks beat every Defense and ignore protection, traps, charms, mirrors and Narrow Escape, so each one kills.
- A Profiler who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the profile op, which spends the token; code tells them the result and tokens left. Don't tell() the Profiler anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- Ritualist who spent tokens (and wasn't role-blocked): compare the guessed role with the target's exact role (a Roleplayer is a Roleplayer). Right: deal the Attack (1 token Standard, 2 Divine). Wrong: no Attack; announce it with tell(['all'], '<name> is a Ritualist.') tonight, which is read out at the start of the next Day, even if the Ritualist dies tonight. Astral Visit.
- Veteran on alert (spent an alert token; set_tokens): Standard Defense, can't be role-blocked, and a Strong Attack on every player who visited them tonight, of any faction, including a role-blocker and the Katana holder if it attacked them. Astral Visits aren't hit. Not a visit. Tell the Veteran whether anyone visited and, if so, how many and whether each attack succeeded (e.g. '2 players visited you: your attack killed one and failed on the other'), never who they were.
- A Vigilante whose shot kills is told the victim's role by code (pass by=<the Vigilante> on the kill op); tell them only whether the attack succeeded and how many tokens they have left.
- Werewolf: on even-numbered Nights only, a Werewolf who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) rampages: at its target's house (a visit to them; put it in record_visits) or, with no target or itself as target, at home (not a visit). Call record_visits first, then the rampage op ({op:'rampage', by, player}, player left out for a home rampage): code lists the Strong Attacks it deals, cause 'Werewolf', from the recorded visits: on the target (a visit) and on every other player who visited the target (or, at home, the Werewolf) tonight, of any faction (not visits; Astral Visits aren't visits, so they aren't hit). Resolve each like any attack (Defense, Medics, charms, traps, mirrors: give the visit flag code gives). An Enforcer counts a rampage at a player's house, its hits on visitors included, as an Attack of the Werewolf's own choosing; a home rampage doesn't count. Tell the Werewolf how many players it attacked and how many of those attacks killed, never who the visitors were (e.g. 'Your rampage attacked 3 players and killed 2').
- Drowsy (a trait, R24): code draws each night whether a Drowsy player is role-blocked; the line below says what it drew tonight. Never roll or decide it yourself.
- Narrow Escape (a hidden trait, R24): resolve every attack as usual (Defense, protection, traps, charms). If after that a holder named below would die tonight from any attack that isn't Divine, they don't die: every non-Divine attack on them tonight fails instead, and you use the narrow_escape op, which uses it up. Tell them and each attacker as for any failed attack; a protector whose protection didn't stop an attack learns nothing from the escape. A Divine attack still kills them: give that kill divine=true (code refuses a night kill of a holder otherwise). A night with no lethal attack doesn't use it. Never mention the trait.
- Paranoid (a trait, R24): code draws each night whether a Paranoid player gets a fake attack; the line below says what it drew tonight. Never roll or decide it yourself.
- Disguised (a trait, R24): every exact-role check (R18: e.g. an Oracle's or Ritualist's guess, a Mortician's clean) sees these players as these Village roles, alive or dead: Frank as Prosecutor; Niaj as Enforcer. Alignment checks still see their true alignment. Never reveal a true role behind a disguise.
- Erin has the hidden Drowsy trait (R24) and is role-blocked tonight; code drew it. Handle it exactly like a role-block (R9) with no blocker: their actions, automatic effects and trait actions have no effect and spend no tokens, they make no visit, and they are told they were role-blocked, as usual. - Grace (Drowsy) is not role-blocked by the trait tonight; code drew it.

Once I was dead I had no further information needs.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
I didn't notice any rule violations. Things I checked:
- Bob's trial at 10-3 matches Bob, me (both Merciful) and Judy voting Innocent.
- The 10 votes from 9 voters on Day 3 and 9 from 8 on Day 4 are both explained by Heidi's public Mayor reveal. Still, the announcement says "a role changed the count on purpose", which is vague and could mislead people even after a confirmed Mayor.
- On Night 3 both Ivan and Dave got Paranoid fake Katana notices after every Yakuza was dead. That is legal but unusual, and it shaped the Day 4 debate. Frank argued that two Paranoids on one night is unlikely, and he happened to be right that it was unusual.
answers.suggestions:
- After a Mayor reveal, have vote announcements say plainly that the Mayor's double vote accounts for the extra count, rather than the generic "a role changed the count" line.
- Add a per-night summary of claimed visits to the public ledger.
- Remind the Yakuza at night that on even nights a Werewolf rampage hits every visitor to its target, the Katana holder included. This matters most for a holder who also visits with their own role.

answers.confusing_rules:
1) The Kitsune's release doesn't say whether it is a visit. As Fortune Teller I had to assume it was one (Dave → Judy on N2) to make my 3/6 count fit. It turned out to be right, but the role text should say so.
2) The Werewolf's attacks on visitors are 'not visits', but it isn't obvious whether the Bloodhound counts them as attacks. Olivia's case against Frank depended on a rampage at one house counting as 2 attacks. 'Attacks they made' should explicitly include rampage hits on visitors, Berserker hits and the like.
3) I had to work out several things for the Fortune Teller myself: does a role-blocked holder's Katana visit count, does a Werewolf at home count, and does a Veteran on alert count? The general rules cover these, but a short FT-specific list of what counts would help, like the Cartographer's note that 'self-visits link no one'.
answers.missing_information: Reconciling my counts meant manually tracking every player's claimed visit each night across long chat logs. The ledger records claims, but not a per-night table of who claims to have visited whom. Whether traits like Paranoid exist is secret by design. That's fine, but two Paranoid holders getting fake Katana notices on the same night (Ivan and Dave on N3) looked like an impossible coincidence, and Frank used it in his defense. Nothing tells players how many traits are 'roughly' in play per kind.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: As a Disguised Fortune Teller, I had no way to back up my claim if an exact-role check showed 'Enforcer'. That's by design, but I'd have liked a way to note the disguise publicly other than my will. Nothing else.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
Nothing looked broken. Every count I got matched the revealed actions: N1 2/3, N2 3/6, N3 2/2. Things that were odd but legal:

answers.suggestions:

- In the Kitsune text, say whether the release is a visit.
- In the Bloodhound text, say explicitly that a Werewolf's hits on visitors and other area attacks each count as an attack.

answers.confusing_rules:
The Bloodhound's 'how many Attacks they have made' was unclear in a few cases. Does a Werewolf rampage that hits a target and a visitor count as 1 Attack or 2? Does a Kitsune releasing a swallowed attack count as the Kitsune's own Attack? Do Veteran or trap hits count? The text lists 'alert or trap hits' but doesn't say anything about multi-target attacks. My whole Day 4 case assumed a rampage counts as 2 and a release as 1. That turned out right, but I had to guess. I'd like an explicit line saying each target hit counts once, with released or reflected attacks credited to the releaser or reflector.

The R4 note '10 votes from 9 voters: a role changed the count on purpose' also showed up when the only cause was a publicly revealed Mayor. That isn't wrong, but the wording made it sound like a hidden manipulator.

The reveal shows both had Paranoid, so it was legitimate, but it looked very suspicious in play, and Frank built his last defense on how unlikely it was. With hand-picked traits, a hidden trait can repeat across players and create coincidences like this.

After Grace was hanged, no Yakuza were left. The game went on only because Frank (the Werewolf) was alive, which matches R1.

2. When the only cause of a changed total is an already-revealed Mayor, say so in the vote-total note instead of the generic 'a role changed the count' message.
3. Give each player a private summary of their own past public claims in the ledger, so bluffs stay consistent.
4. Let players attach their own result lines to the will with one click.

answers.confusing_rules:
These are the rules I had to interpret as moderator:
1) The Bloodhound's token "track". The rules never say whether picking a player for a triad is a visit. The free random triad clearly isn't one. I used the default (a visit), so Olivia→Dave on N2 and Olivia→Frank on N3 counted in Niaj's Fortune Teller numbers and in Carol's map. Players worked this out correctly, but the decision rests on a default rather than on text.
2) What counts as an attack for the Bloodhound. I counted the Werewolf's rampage hit on a visitor (Mallory) as one of Frank's attacks, so Frank had 2 after N2. I counted Dave's release as Dave's attack and the swallowed Katana as Bob's. The Bloodhound text lists "Katana attacks, shots, alert or trap hits" but doesn't mention rampage hits on visitors, swallowed attacks or released attacks.
3) A Katana holder who dies the same night. Mallory held the Katana, attacked Carol and was killed by the Werewolf. R8 says the attack is dealt by "whoever holds it at the end of the night", and R8 also says a dead holder passes it on only after the night's results. I resolved both attacks at the same time, so Mallory's hit landed and the Katana then went to Grace. Saying this outright in R8 would help.
4) Who can get Stocked: "a role that starts with tokens and can ever have more than it starts with". As far as I can tell, no role or effect in these rules ever gives a token back (the Magpie only takes them). Read literally, nobody qualifies, but Carol was dealt Stocked anyway (her Cartographer started with 3 map tokens).
5) Ritualist against a Disguised target. Grace's N2 guess "Niaj = Fortune Teller" was right about his real role, but Niaj was Disguised as Enforcer, so the exact-role check would have failed and outed her as a Ritualist. A Drowsy block meant it never mattered. The rules do cover this, but only through the general R19 wording, and it's very easy to miss.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
I wanted to check a night's results for consistency (visits against counts against groups) before sending them out. Two cases where this would have helped:
- On N3 I'd have liked to check whether a Paranoid fake Katana notice made sense when no Yakuza were left alive. All three Yakuza were dead after Grace's hanging on Day 3, but Dave and Ivan both got fake Katana-survival notices on N3.
- Ivan was on alert and was told "nobody visited you". Sending him a Katana-survival notice the same night gave away that the notice was fake.
I couldn't adjust or suppress either notice under the rules as written.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
No resolution errors that I could find. Votes, counts, map sizes, Mayor double votes, the Faultline result, Drowsy refunds and the winner list all check out. Oddities:
1) Both Paranoid players (Dave and Ivan) fired on the same night (a 1/16 chance), and both notices were Katana ones while no Yakuza were alive. Frank used the double fake in his defence ("two Paranoids at once is a stretch"). This was legal, but the fake-attack generator ignores the game state.
2) A Paranoid Veteran on alert gets "nobody visited you" plus "the Katana attacked you". Those two messages contradict each other, which exposes the hidden trait at once.
3) Feedback after a role-block is inconsistent. Grace's message said "2 ritual tokens left"; Erin's two blocked messages (N1 and N3) gave no token count at all.
4) The vote-count note "10 votes from 9 voters: a role changed the count on purpose" appeared even though the doubling came from a Mayor who had already been publicly revealed. It's true, but unnecessary.
5) Bob's failed-Katana message had "You still have 1 oath token" tacked on, even though the oath had nothing to do with that night.
answers.suggestions:
- Give the moderator a per-night resolution sheet: the visit list, Fortune Teller and Cartographer values computed automatically, the Bloodhound attack ledger, a token ledger, and the factions still alive.
- Tie Paranoid fakes to the game state: no Katana fakes once no Yakuza are alive, and no fake hit on a Veteran who was on alert that night.
- State outright that the Bloodhound's track is (or isn't) a visit, and list which attacks count for it: rampage hits on visitors and released attacks.
- Reword Stocked's eligibility, or name the roles that qualify.
- Make block feedback uniform: always or never include tokens left.
- Add an R8 example of a holder who attacks and dies on the same night.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: If your charm swallows a Katana attack, release it the next night on a suspect who has already broken their own claim (here, a Defense claim that didn't add up). Then post the release openly. It accounts for the extra 'Katana' attack in the counts, so nobody can pin a later Katana death on you.

Line up the Fortune Teller's visited/visitor counts with every claimed visit for that night. Once the visited set is full, any role-block or attack a player claims that nobody's visit explains is either a hidden-trait effect (Drowsy, Paranoid) or a lie. Seeing which one usually decides the vote.

Treat a lone 'attacked with the Katana and survived' notice with no visit to back it as likely fake, from the hidden Paranoid trait. This applies when the counts have no slot for that visit, or when a player on alert saw no visitors. Several players can have Paranoid in the same game, so two fake notices on one night are possible.

A Disguised killer passes exact-role checks under their cover. Use attack-count results (Bloodhound) and visit math to catch them, not role checks. A count that goes up between nights for someone claiming a role with no attack is a strong mechanical case.
After a hang you expect to end the game, say beforehand: 'if the game doesn't end, someone is still hiding.' That gives the town a check it can use right away whatever the outcome.

tips_feedback.tip: Hang on a mechanical case (corroborated lone visitor to a victim, etc.)
tips_feedback.why: Carol's map plus my charm claim got Bob hanged on Day 2. Olivia's attack count then got Frank, the Werewolf, hanged on Day 4. Both were mechanical cases, and they won the game.

tips_feedback.tip: Surviving an attack proves little (Paranoid fake notices, Narrow Escape...)
tips_feedback.why: On Night 3, Ivan and I both got fake Katana-survival notices from Paranoid. Using Niaj's 2/2 counts, the town correctly wrote them off instead of hanging either of us.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't announce tonight's target, or even that you will act
tips_feedback.why: I never announced where I would release my swallowed attack, so Judy, the Jester, was killed at night instead of getting a hanging.

tips_feedback.tip: An Evil read can come from a Jester... Usually leave a likely Jester alive
tips_feedback.why: Everyone avoided hanging Judy even though her Defense claim kept escalating. She was killed at night, so the Jester never got her win or her revenge.

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Map the player most likely to be attacked (the loudest early reader, or the target of a Day-1 push). The group around an attack target is tiny, and if the survivor or a protector confirms the attack, that group names the holder. Post the exact names and sizes the moment a vote hinges on them.

A dead player's will can be forged by a Fabricator. Check each will's night claims against the public visit counts (Fortune Teller, Cartographer sizes, Bloodhound token visits). A will that names a visit the counts don't allow, or that conveniently backs a dead suspect's accusation, is a lie or a forgery. Use it as evidence against whoever it shields.

After a public claim that hangs a Yakuza, expect to die that night. Post any result you might get later in public that same Day, and write tonight's planned target and what each result would mean into your will. That way a forged or cleaned will is easier for the town to spot as off-pattern.

Understating your remaining tokens in public (e.g. a Bloodhound saying '0 tokens' while holding one) keeps the Katana off you and can hide a decisive check. Say why when you reveal it, so it isn't read as a broken claim.

Count night attacks per player: a Bloodhound total minus everyone's claimed shots and releases gives a lone player's attack count. A no-action claimant with 2 attacks on the night of a two-victim rampage is a Werewolf. That is a mechanical case worth a hang over any 'my word against yours' clash.

tips_feedback.tip: Hang on a mechanical case: ... a corroborated lone visitor to a victim.
tips_feedback.why: My map (Judy's group = Bob, Dave, Judy), Dave's charm claim and Niaj's 2/3 counts left Bob as the only possible Katana visitor. Town hanged him 10-3, and he was Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't hint at your role on Days 1–2. Once a result bears on a vote, post the night, target and exact result right away.
tips_feedback.why: I claimed with the full map on Day 2, before Bob claimed. That made his counter-claim look reactive and won the vote.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens early, because they die with you.
tips_feedback.why: Olivia did the opposite. She held her last scent token and publicly said she had 0, and that hidden token is what caught the Werewolf on N3. Hiding a token can beat spending it early.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't defend a doomed teammate, because hidden Innocent votes show up in the totals.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory defended Bob and stated an Innocent vote. On Day 3 that, plus her impossible will, marked her as the N2 Katana holder after her death.

tips_feedback.tip: First kill the players whose next result could still expose you: Census Takers, Cartographers, Fortune Tellers...
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza followed it and killed me on N2, and my N2 map never reached the town. But Fortune Teller counts still exposed the forged will, so killing just one visit-info role wasn't enough for them.

If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: If you go on alert and the result says 'nobody visited you' but you also get an 'attacked and survived' notice, the notice is fake (the hidden Paranoid trait). Every non-astral attack is a visit. Post both results together at once, and put them in your will. They clear you and defuse the 'survived on innate Defense = Werewolf' case.

Treat the Fortune Teller's visited and visitor counts as a constraint puzzle. Give each claimed visit a slot, and add the Katana holder plus any rampage. A dead player's will or a living player's claim that needs an extra visit the counts don't allow is a lie. Remember that a self-only or astral action (Cartographer map, Oracle, Veteran alert) takes no slot.

To find a Werewolf, use the attack-count results (Bloodhound): a rampage at a house scores one attack per victim. Then narrow the pool to players who claim no visit on the full-moon night. Also remember the Werewolf can't act on odd nights, so the hang before an even night matters most.

Saying you have 0 tokens left to keep the Katana off you can work. But the result you later reveal from the hidden token will be attacked as 'you said 0'. Have the explanation ready ('Bloodhounds start with 2, and I hid one') and post it as soon as you're challenged.

In hand-picked setups with many traits, two players can get fake Paranoid notices on the same night. Don't treat 'two fake notices at once' as impossible. Check every notice against the visit counts instead.

tips_feedback.tip: Surviving an attack proves little ... a fake Paranoid notice
tips_feedback.why: Dave and I both got fake Katana-survival notices on N3. Frank tried to use mine as proof that I was the Werewolf. My alert result plus Niaj's 2/2 count showed the notice was fake, and the town didn't fall for it.

tips_feedback.tip: Hang on a mechanical case
tips_feedback.why: All three hangs came from mechanics: Bob on Carol's map plus Dave's charm, Grace on a block nothing could explain once Niaj's visited set was full, and Frank on Olivia's attack count. All three were Evil or the Werewolf, and the town won.

tips_feedback.tip: Agree each member's cover ... Check the cover against every posted visit result
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza didn't do this check, and it cost them. Mallory's forged and own wills claimed visits that broke Niaj's counts, which exposed her as the N2 holder. That shows how much the check matters.

tips_feedback.tip: Post important results in public while you are still alive
tips_feedback.why: Niaj, Olivia and Alice posted their results quickly. Alice's Jester result broke Judy's Defense claim, and Olivia's count settled the case on Frank before the full moon.

tips_feedback.why: Killing Carol (Cartographer) on N2 was right, since her map is what caught Bob. But my backup ritual on the Fortune Teller was stopped by Drowsy, and he went on to build the cases against me and others.

tips_feedback.tip: Agree each member's cover in Night 1 chat: a real Village role that fits your tokens and real visits...
tips_feedback.why: Bob's Lookout cover, 'only visitor = Dave', clashed head-on with a real Kitsune and a Cartographer map, and Judy's Jester claim couldn't save it. Covers that claim a specific visit result can be broken when a real protector is at the same target.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens early, because they die with you.
tips_feedback.why: Others used it well: Alice spent all her Vigilante tokens on N2 and got the Jester read that broke Bob's defense. Bob ignored it and died with his oath token unspent. I held my ritual on N1 and then lost N2 to a block, so I died with 2 tokens.

tips_feedback.tip: An Evil read or a caught lie can come from a Jester... Usually leave a likely Jester alive.
tips_feedback.why: The town shot the likely Jester (Judy) at night, which carries no Jester revenge, and the role it revealed confirmed Dave's story. Here, killing her at night was clearly better than leaving her alive.

lessons.tip: Build a visit ledger for each night from the Fortune Teller's numbers. Put every claimed visit in it, including token uses like a Bloodhound pick, a Kitsune charm or a profile. If a claimed attack would push the visited or visitor count past the FT's numbers, the attack notice was fake (Paranoid). More than one player can be Paranoid on the same night, so 'two fake notices is unlikely' is a weak counterargument.

After each hang or night death, check whether the game ended. If the game goes on after a hang, a win-blocking enemy (Yakuza or a Neutral killer) is still alive. So if every Yakuza lead is gone and the game keeps going, look for a Neutral killer. A clean count on someone's attacks (Bloodhound) plus a rampage-sized death pattern is enough to hang on.

Reveal when your double vote decides a close hang, or when removing yourself from a suspect pool settles the case. In this game that was Day 3, when the Werewolf pool was down to the players who claimed no visit. Revealing earlier only makes you a Katana target. Revealing later wastes the votes and leaves you looking like a no-visit Neutral killer suspect.

Don't swap a clean fit for a speculative one. On Day 3 I suggested that Mallory had blocked Erin as a Pharmacist, but Carol's sizes and the FT's N1 counts already fit Mallory→Carol plus a Drowsy block with no visitor. Extra theories confuse the town and hand liars cover. Check them against every count before you post.

Under-reporting how many tokens you have left (Olivia said '0 tokens' while still holding one) keeps the Katana and Pharmacist off you. If you do it, explain the lie right away when you post the later result, so it doesn't read as a made-up claim. Bloodhounds start with 2 tokens, so the town can check that the numbers add up.

tips_feedback.tip: Surviving an attack proves little... fake Paranoid notice
tips_feedback.why: Ivan and Dave both got fake Katana survival notices on N3 (both were Paranoid) after all the Yakuza were dead. With this tip in mind we treated those notices as fake, which the FT counts confirmed. That stopped us hanging Ivan, which was the Werewolf's whole defense.

tips_feedback.tip: Hang on a mechanical case (corroborated lone visitor, results that break a claim)
tips_feedback.why: Bob was hanged on Carol's map plus Dave's charm, and Frank on Olivia's Bloodhound count against the size of the rampage. Both were correct hangs, built on mechanics rather than vibes.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't defend a doomed teammate; vote Guilty and say so
tips_feedback.why: For the Yakuza: Grace voted Guilty on Bob and stayed clean on Day 2. Mallory's public Innocent (she was forced by Merciful) became one of the main points against her after she died, which shows the cost of not following it.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't announce tonight's target, or even that you will act
tips_feedback.why: Olivia hid both her last token and her N3 target. She got a clean count on Frank that nobody could pre-empt, and that decided Day 4.

tips_feedback.tip: Hunt Neutral killers on purpose; read every cause of death
tips_feedback.why: The Werewolf cause on Carol and Mallory showed a Neutral killer was alive. The town narrowed the suspects to the players who claimed no visit and hanged Frank before the full moon on N4.

lessons.tip: If you go on alert and the result says 'nobody visited you' but you also get an 'attacked and survived' notice, the notice is fake (the hidden Paranoid trait). Every non-astral attack is a visit. Post both results together at once, and put them in your will. They clear you and defuse the 'survived on innate Defense = Werewolf' case.

Treat the Fortune Teller's visited and visitor counts as a constraint puzzle. Give each claimed visit a slot, and add the Katana holder plus any rampage. A dead player's will or a living player's claim that needs an extra visit the counts don't allow is a lie. Remember that a self-only or astral action (Cartographer map, Oracle, Veteran alert) takes no slot.

To find a Werewolf, use the attack-count results (Bloodhound): a rampage at a house scores one attack per victim. Then narrow the pool to players who claim no visit on the full-moon night. Also remember the Werewolf can't act on odd nights, so the hang before an even night matters most.

Saying you have 0 tokens left to keep the Katana off you can work. But the result you later reveal from the hidden token will be attacked as 'you said 0'. Have the explanation ready ('Bloodhounds start with 2, and I hid one') and post it as soon as you're challenged.

In hand-picked setups with many traits, two players can get fake Paranoid notices on the same night. Don't treat 'two fake notices at once' as impossible. Check every notice against the visit counts instead.

tips_feedback.tip: Surviving an attack proves little ... a fake Paranoid notice
tips_feedback.why: Dave and I both got fake Katana-survival notices on N3. Frank tried to use mine as proof that I was the Werewolf. My alert result plus Niaj's 2/2 count showed the notice was fake, and the town didn't fall for it.

tips_feedback.tip: Hang on a mechanical case
tips_feedback.why: All three hangs came from mechanics: Bob on Carol's map plus Dave's charm, Grace on a block nothing could explain once Niaj's visited set was full, and Frank on Olivia's attack count. All three were Evil or the Werewolf, and the town won.

tips_feedback.tip: Agree each member's cover ... Check the cover against every posted visit result
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza didn't do this check, and it cost them. Mallory's forged and own wills claimed visits that broke Niaj's counts, which exposed her as the N2 holder. That shows how much the check matters.

tips_feedback.tip: Post important results in public while you are still alive
tips_feedback.why: Niaj, Olivia and Alice posted their results quickly. Alice's Jester result broke Judy's Defense claim, and Olivia's count settled the case on Frank before the full moon.

lessons.tip: Never fake-claim a Neutral killer (for example 'Standard Defense'). It makes you the top target for a Vigilante shot or a stored Kitsune attack at night, and dying at night is a loss. Fake-claim something whose only fix is a Day hang, such as a Yakuza-only role or a broken Village claim, so a hanging is the obvious answer and a night kill isn't.

Make your suspicious move early on a Day that still has trials left, then nominate yourself or get someone to nominate you that same Day. If you only look guilty after the Day's hang is settled, the town gets a whole night to shoot you instead.
Pick one fake claim and stick to it. Changing your story ('thanks, Medic', then 'innate Defense', then 'Standard') was read openly as Jester baiting, and the town then refused to hang me.

A Kitsune holding a swallowed attack is a live killer. They will usually release it on the town's top suspect the next night. Treat that suspect as being in night danger, and count the release as an extra possible Katana death.
Being loudly contrarian on Day 1 made me the Yakuza's first Katana target. Save the attention-seeking for Days that have trials, when it can actually get you hanged.

tips_feedback.tip: Usually leave a likely Jester alive. If you do hang one, keep the Guilty votes to a bare majority.
tips_feedback.why: Several players (Erin, Niaj, Olivia) called my changing claims Jester baiting. The town would not hang me and killed me at night instead, so I lost. Following the tip worked for them.

tips_feedback.tip: Surviving an attack proves little... a survivor who confirms the survival under a claim with no Defense fits a Serial Killer.
tips_feedback.why: The town correctly worked out that Basic Defense can't stop a Standard Katana hit, so my claim meant either a Neutral killer or a lie. That pushed Alice into a Strong night shot, which cost me the game.

tips_feedback.tip: Hang on a mechanical case, e.g. a corroborated lone visitor to a victim.
tips_feedback.why: Carol's map plus Dave's charm caught Bob, the Katana holder, on Day 2, even though I tried to muddy it by claiming Defense.

tips_feedback.tip: Vigilante: by Day 2–3, fire a Basic shot on a real lead.
tips_feedback.why: Alice spent all 3 tokens on a Strong shot at me, a Jester who blocks nobody's win. She could have saved them for the Werewolf.

lessons.tip: If a Fortune Teller or Cartographer is posting counts, a fake visit claim adds a visited player. Claim a target who was really visited that night (e.g. your own Katana victim) and give a result that fits, such as 'Carol visited no one' for an Astral-acting Cartographer. Naming a quiet bystander to avoid being placed at the body gets broken as soon as the counts and the other visitors' claims come out.

lessons.applies_to: Yakuza writing a will with a fake result
lessons.tip: Before you lock in a fake will result, check whether the person you name could have visited that night (Bloodhound tokens, Profiler, other trackers). 'X visited no one' is a strong, checkable statement. Pick a target who is hard to verify, or say 'no result / blocked' if the counts leave room for a blocker.

lessons.applies_to: Yakuza with Merciful (or any vote that always counts Innocent)
lessons.tip: Your trial vote counts Innocent no matter what, so don't add public arguments for a doomed teammate. Speak for the town's case, or stay quiet. The Innocent tally plus a teammate-friendly 'I lean the other guy' got me named as the next holder the moment my will slipped.

lessons.applies_to: Yakuza whose night action got blocked by Drowsy
lessons.tip: If the public counts already fill the visited set, 'I was role-blocked with no visitor' is the story nobody can check, and it gets you hanged. With an Astral cover role (Oracle), report a plausible wrong guess instead. An unconfirmable miss is safer than an unexplained block.

lessons.applies_to: Yakuza on even nights with a Werewolf possible
lessons.tip: On full-moon nights, the strongest information role (the Cartographer who just exposed you) is also a likely Werewolf rampage target. Every visitor dies, including the Katana holder and anyone doing a frame or forge. If a Neutral killer is suspected, think about hitting a less obvious target on even nights, or keep the holder's visit separate from other actions.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't defend a doomed teammate, because hidden Innocent votes show up in the totals.
tips_feedback.why: I ignored it. I argued that Bob's story held up and said I leaned Dave, and that Innocent was later used as evidence that I was the N2 holder. Following it would have kept me cleaner.

tips_feedback.tip: Agree each member's cover in Night 1 chat... Check the cover against every posted visit result.
tips_feedback.why: My N2 will ('tracked Olivia, she visited no one') failed this check. Olivia's Bloodhound visit and Niaj's full visited set broke it, which proved the will was fake and marked me as Yakuza after I died.

tips_feedback.tip: Avoid PMs between teammates by Day.
tips_feedback.why: We sent no PMs between teammates, so no Yakuza connection came from the PM ledger. Our exposure came only from claims and counts.

tips_feedback.tip: First kill the players whose next result could still expose you: Census Takers, Cartographers, Fortune Tellers...
tips_feedback.why: Killing Carol (the Cartographer) and sending the ritual at Niaj (the Fortune Teller) were the right targets. They failed because of the Werewolf and Grace's Drowsy block, not because the priority was wrong.

tips_feedback.tip: Hang on a mechanical case... a corroborated lone visitor to a victim.
tips_feedback.why: For the town it worked: Carol's map, Dave's charm and Niaj's counts gave a mechanical case that hanged Bob. Bob's Lookout counter-claim couldn't beat a map that had both of them in Judy's group.

lessons.tip: Your two counts are only useful once every living player has said what they did that night. Wait for all of those claims before you fill your visited and visitor slots with guesses. On D4 I filled my 2/2 with the Katana hitting Ivan plus a Pharmacist on Erin, and I leaned Ivan. Then Olivia revealed a token visit she had kept hidden, and that explanation fell apart. List the claimed visits first and only then look for what's left over.

Visit counts are the best way to break a forged or false will. Mallory's will said she 'tracked Olivia', but the visited set (Carol, Judy, Dave) had no room for that visit, which put her at the body. Every night, check each dead player's claimed visit against the Fortune Teller, Cartographer and Bloodhound numbers.

A Disguised player can safely claim their true role publicly. The Ritualist's guess is an exact-role check, so it sees the disguise: guessing the claimed role fails and the moderator announces the Ritualist publicly. As a Ritualist, remember that any claimant might be Disguised, so don't spend a guess on a single claim with nothing else backing it.

Several players can have Paranoid in the same game, because traits are picked by hand and there are about 13–15 of them. If two players report surviving a Katana attack on the same night and the visit counts have no room for either attack, believe the counts. Frank's 'two Paranoids is unlikely' was a trap: both notices really were fake.

Claiming 0 tokens left can keep the Katana off you, and you can then spend the hidden token on a lead. Olivia did this and caught the Werewolf. When you reveal the hidden token, say up front why you lied so the change in your claim doesn't get you hanged.

tips_feedback.tip: Hang on a mechanical case (corroborated lone visitor to a victim, etc.)
tips_feedback.why: Carol's map plus Dave's charm got Bob hanged. My Fortune Teller counts broke Mallory's will and Grace's block story. Olivia's Bloodhound count caught Frank. All three hangs hit non-Village players.

tips_feedback.tip: Surviving an attack proves little (... a fake Paranoid notice)
tips_feedback.why: Ivan and Dave both got fake Katana-survival notices on N3 because both had Paranoid. Trusting the visit counts over the notices kept us from hanging Ivan, which was what Frank wanted.

tips_feedback.tip: Once a result bears on a vote, post the night, target and exact result right away
tips_feedback.why: Posting my N1 2/3 on Day 2 pinned down who visited Judy and forced Erin to explain her block. Posting my N2 3/6 exposed Mallory's lie in her will.

tips_feedback.tip: Agree each member's cover ... Check the cover against every posted visit result
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza didn't do this: Mallory's forged will and Tracker cover contradicted my public counts, which pinned the N2 Katana holder on her and made Grace's no-visitor block look unexplained.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens early, because they die with you
tips_feedback.why: Olivia's best move was to hold her last Bloodhound token and claim 0 tokens, and that caught the Werewolf. Holding a token while lying about the count can beat spending it early.

lessons.tip: Your counts are cumulative, so treat them as equations. Once some attacks are public (a Vigilante's claimed shot, a Kitsune's claimed release), subtract them from a triad total to get one player's count. Spend a token on an unexplained no-visit claimant: a jump from 0 to 2 attacks in one triad matches a Werewolf rampage (target plus visitor) and shows the claim is false.

Saying publicly that you have 0 tokens left keeps the Katana and blockers off your last token. When you post the result later, say straight away why you hid it and remind people of the starting count (Bloodhounds start with 2). Then the change in your story reads as caution, not fabrication.

Line up every claimed visit against the Fortune Teller's visited and visitor counts each night. When the visited set is full, any claimed visit to someone else is false, and so is any claimed 'block by a visitor'. A will that says 'tracked X, no visits' breaks once X's own visit is confirmed. This caught a forged or false Yakuza will in this game.

Several hidden Paranoid traits can appear in the same game. Two players getting fake Katana survival notices on the same night is quite possible when the FT counts leave no room for the attacks. Trust the visit math over 'two Paranoids is too unlikely'.

Causes of death come in pairs: a victim killed by Katana + Werewolf plus a second victim killed by the Werewolf alone means the Werewolf rampaged at the first victim's house and the second victim was visiting there. That visitor was often the Katana holder.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't announce tonight's target, or even that you will act, in public or by PM.
tips_feedback.why: I hid my last scent token by claiming 0 tokens on D3. That kept the Katana off me, and the N3 token on Frank caught the Werewolf before the full moon.

tips_feedback.tip: Hunt Neutral killers on purpose. Read every cause of death.
tips_feedback.why: The 'Werewolf' causes on Carol and Mallory showed a rampage at Carol's house. That narrowed the Werewolf to the players claiming no visits and told me where to spend my token.

tips_feedback.tip: Surviving an attack proves little. It can come from ... a fake Paranoid notice.
tips_feedback.why: Ivan and Dave were both hidden Paranoid. Town accepted their notices as fake because the FT 2/2 count had no room for a real Katana hit, so we didn't mislynch Ivan as the Werewolf.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens early, because they die with you.
tips_feedback.why: Holding my second token to N3, behind a 0-tokens bluff, did better than spending it early. Once a Werewolf was known to exist, a later token aimed at the unexplained claimants was worth more.

tips_feedback.tip: Agree each member's cover in Night 1 chat ... Check the cover against every posted visit result.
tips_feedback.why: For the Yakuza this mattered when they ignored it. Mallory's will said 'tracked Olivia, no visits', but my token visit to Dave broke it against Niaj's counts. That exposed her as the holder and made the case against the Yakuza easier.

summary: The Village won because three results kept backing each other up. On Night 1, Carol's map of Judy showed only Bob, Dave and Judy, Dave claimed his fox charm swallowed the Katana attack, and Niaj's Fortune Teller counts (2 visited, 3 visitors) left no room for anyone else. Bob's Lookout cover ("only Dave visited") needed Judy to have her own Defense. Judy was the Jester and claimed Standard Defense to bait a hanging, but town read that as a Neutral killer or a lie and hanged Bob 10-3. Mallory's public lean towards Dave and her Innocent vote marked her too. On Night 2 the Yakuza fell apart. Alice's 3-token Strong Vigilante shot killed Judy and revealed her as the Jester, which confirmed Dave. Frank, the Werewolf, rampaged at Carol's house and also killed Mallory, the Katana holder visiting Carol. Grace's Ritualist guess on Niaj was stopped by her own hidden Drowsy trait. Mallory's will, written before the night, said "tracked Olivia, she visited no one", and Olivia's Bloodhound token visit proved it false. Her forged will for Carol, pointing at Dave, convinced no one. On Day 3, Niaj's full list of who was visited on Night 2 meant nobody could have blocked Grace, so her "Oracle, blocked with no visitor" claim got the last Yakuza hanged. Olivia had hidden her last Bloodhound token by claiming 0 on Day 3. On Night 3 she spent it on Frank, and subtracting known attacks showed he had made exactly the 2 attacks of a rampage at a house. He was hanged on Day 4 before the full moon. Fortune Teller counts also showed that the attack notices Ivan and Dave got on Night 3 were fake (Paranoid).

lessons.tip: When a public visit result has already put you at a victim's house, pick a cover role whose story explains the outcome everyone saw on its own. For example, a protector explains a failed kill. Don't pick one that needs an extra, unprovable assumption, such as the victim having their own Defense.
lessons.evidence: Bob was placed at Judy's house by Carol's map. He claimed Lookout and said he saw only Dave. That story only worked if Judy had her own Defense, while Dave's charm explained her survival by itself. Heidi pointed out that a 'Bob protected Judy' claim would have made it a real Bob-against-Dave contest. Bob was hanged 10-3.

lessons.tip: Don't write a fake result into your will before the night resolves, and never claim that another player 'visited no one'. Many roles visit by spending a token (Bloodhound, Profiler, Chronicler), so the claim is easy to disprove. If you must fake a result, make it one that the public counts can't contradict.
lessons.evidence: Mallory's will said 'N2: tracked Olivia. She visited no one.' Olivia had spent a Bloodhound token on Dave, and Niaj's list of who was visited on Night 2 (Carol, Judy, Dave) left no room for Mallory to have tracked anyone. Her will was called false straight away, and she was named as the Katana holder.

lessons.tip: Combine the Fortune Teller's two counts with every claimed visit to list exactly who was visited and who visited each night. Once that list is full, it exposes fake results, confirms or rules out blockers, and shows which attack notices were fake (Paranoid).
lessons.evidence: Night 2 (3 visited, 6 visitors) left nobody who could have blocked Grace and broke Mallory's will. Night 3 (2 visited, 2 visitors) was filled by Olivia's visit to Frank and Dave's charm on Heidi. That showed the Katana notices Ivan and Dave got were fake (both had Paranoid) and disproved Frank's 'Ivan survived a real hit' defense.

lessons.tip: Understating how many tokens you have left can protect your last one from the Katana. Spend it on your top suspect and explain the lie as soon as the result is in. Subtract known attacks from a Bloodhound count to pin the rest on one player.
lessons.evidence: Olivia claimed '0 tokens' on Day 3, survived, then spent her last token on Frank. Dave, Erin and Frank had made 3 attacks; Dave had 1 and Erin 0, so Frank had 2, exactly a rampage at Carol's with Mallory visiting. Frank tried to discredit her over the token lie, but the Mayor's double vote and the others backed her, and Frank was hanged.

lessons.applies_to: Yakuza / anyone with an unverifiable claim
lessons.tip: Don't volunteer an oddity nobody can check, such as 'I was blocked with no visitor', when the public visit counts can rule out a blocker. A plain, quiet result (or no action) draws less suspicion than an anomaly the counts can't explain.
lessons.evidence: Grace claimed Oracle and added that she was blocked on Night 2 with no visitor. Niaj's full list of who was visited meant nothing could explain the block, and she was hanged 9-1. Erin's identical Night 1 Drowsy claim had been accepted only because the Night 1 counts left room for a blocker.

lessons.tip: When a suspect claims Defense of a certain level, shoot above it. A shot that kills reveals the role, which can settle earlier disputes between claims. Don't save tokens you might die holding.
lessons.evidence: Judy claimed Standard Defense. Alice spent all 3 tokens on a Strong shot, killed her, and learned she was the Jester. That disproved Bob's Defense explanation after the fact, confirmed Dave, and removed a Jester at night, when she couldn't win.

lessons.tip: Escalating Defense claims to bait a hanging tends to get you shot at night, not hanged, especially when a Vigilante or a killer is alive. Make yourself look like a Day-hang target (shaky votes, a slip about your claimed role) rather than a dangerous Neutral killer.
lessons.evidence: Judy went from thanking a Medic to 'innate Defense' to 'Standard Defense'. Town hanged Bob instead, Alice shot her that night, and she lost as the Jester.

lessons.tip: When a teammate is clearly doomed by results that agree with each other, don't publicly lean towards saving them. Your stated lean, plus Innocent votes shown in the totals, makes you the next lead.
lessons.evidence: Mallory argued that 'one detail favors Bob' and that she would hang Dave instead. The 3 Innocent votes were Bob, Judy and Mallory. Frank and Heidi later cited 'her Innocent on Bob' when naming her as the Night 2 holder.

tips_feedback.tip: Vigilante: Dying with unspent shots is the usual failure. By Day 2–3, fire a Basic shot on a real lead...
tips_feedback.why: Alice fired on Night 2 at the player whose own claim had broken (Judy's escalating Defense claim). She used Strong rather than Basic because of the claimed Defense, killed the Jester, and her role result confirmed Dave and the Bob hanging.

tips_feedback.tip: Surviving an attack proves little... But a survivor who confirms the survival under a claim with no Defense, with no protector claiming the save, fits a Serial Killer.
tips_feedback.why: Town reasoned that Basic Defense can't stop a Standard Katana hit, so Judy's Standard claim meant a Neutral killer or a lie. They didn't let it save Bob, and it led to Alice's shot. The same tip's point about fake Paranoid notices helped town discount Ivan's and Dave's Night 3 notices.

tips_feedback.tip: Hang on a mechanical case... a corroborated lone visitor to a victim.
tips_feedback.why: Both Village hangings rested on mechanics. Bob was hanged on Carol's map, Dave's charm and Niaj's counts, and Frank on Olivia's Bloodhound count after subtracting known attacks. Both were correct.

tips_feedback.tip: Hunt Neutral killers on purpose. Read every cause of death...
tips_feedback.why: The 'Werewolf' cause of death on Night 2 started a deliberate Werewolf hunt that narrowed the pool to players who claimed no visit. Olivia spent her last token on that pool and town hanged Frank before the full moon.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't defend a doomed teammate, because hidden Innocent votes show up in the totals.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory ignored this. Her public lean towards Bob plus her Innocent vote, which matched the 3 Innocents, were later used to name her as a Yakuza holder. Following the tip would have protected her.

tips_feedback.tip: Each night, write tonight's planned target in your will and what each possible result would mean.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory applied this to a fake cover and wrote a made-up Night 2 result ('tracked Olivia, she visited no one') before the night resolved. Olivia's real visit disproved it publicly once Mallory died.

tips_feedback.tip: First kill the players whose next result could still expose you: Census Takers, Cartographers, Fortune Tellers...
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza followed it on Night 2 (Katana on Carol, ritual on Niaj). Carol died before her Night 2 map could be posted, but Drowsy stopped the guess on Niaj, and his surviving counts later broke both Mallory's will and Grace's claim. The priority was correct.

issues.description: The program refused end_phase twice because the moderator's private message (tell) went beyond what the rules allow. Night 1: its message to Erin was held. Night 3: its message to Dave and Erin was held. In both cases the players had been hit by hidden traits (Erin's Drowsy role-block; Dave's Paranoid fake attack). The held text isn't in the log, but it probably said too much, for example naming a hidden trait or the source of the block. The program caught this and the messages that were resent were correct, so nothing leaked. Still, the moderator twice tried to send more than the rules allow.

The Bloodhound counts 'how many Attacks' a player has made, but the rules don't clearly say whether one Werewolf rampage that hits the target and a visitor is one Attack or several. The moderator counted Frank's rampage at Carol's as 2 (Carol and Mallory). That fits the Werewolf text ('deal a Strong Attack to them and to every other player who visits'). This count was the sole basis for the Day 4 hanging, and players had to assume it ('A Werewolf rampage at Carol's makes exactly 2 attacks'). One line in the Bloodhound text would remove the doubt.

The Bloodhound's paid tracking ('may also spend a token to track one player') doesn't say whether it is a visit or an Astral Visit. The moderator treated it as a visit (Olivia counted in the Fortune Teller numbers on Night 2 and Night 3). Players' Day 4 reasoning about Niaj's 2/2 depended on this. It is consistent with the default that night actions are visits, but the role text should say so, as other token-tracking roles do.
